Welcome to ADDDitive!

👋 Hi there,

After a month away from LinkedIn, spent partly in New York exploring some of the world’s most inspiring buildings, I have come back with a fresh perspective. Taking time out wasn’t about slowing down; it was about stepping back to reset, reflect, and return with clarity.

That pause reminded me of something critical: in architecture and technology alike, progress doesn’t come from running faster on the same track. It comes from lifting our heads, seeing the bigger picture, and asking better questions.

In this edition, I’ll share the lessons I took from that time away, on wellbeing, strategy, AI adoption, and the rise of ConTech. I’ll also give you a glimpse of what’s coming up this month: free access to my 1,600+ ConTech software database, a new resource on how to move into ConTech careers, and practical templates to help architects build AI strategies that actually work.

The pace of change in our industry is accelerating. My aim here is to cut through the noise, highlight what matters, and help you navigate the opportunities, whether you’re running a practice, building technology, or considering a new career in ConTech.

As always, if you’ve got questions or just want to talk tech and design, hit reply, I’d love to hear from you!

Allister

1. I was off LinkedIn during the whole of August – here’s what I learnt…

A month away (including time in New York exploring great architecture) gave me space to reflect. 

It reminded me that stepping back isn’t about slowing down, it’s about resetting to move forward with clarity.

Here are a few lessons that matter not just personally, but for our industry too:

Image

Health & wellbeing fuel better strategies
Overload leads to short-term thinking. Creating space allows us to see the bigger picture; in business, design, and technology adoption.

Architects need an AI strategy, not just AI tools
The conversations I’m having show that many practices may be dabbling with AI, but few have a clear roadmap. Just as buildings need a design, AI adoption needs structure.

AI Tech Stacks are becoming real
Rather than relying on one “all-in-one” legacy platform, firms should explore lean, interconnected stacks of new tools. These stacks aren’t just experiments, they’re proving to be faster, greener, and more client-focused.

ConTech is booming
The pace of new startups, new roles, and new jobs in ConTech is accelerating, I have over 50 to add to @aec tech jobs. This will create opportunities for architects and AEC professionals to move into emerging areas from AI product management to design automation.

Inspiration fuels innovation
Walking through great buildings reminded me that technology should always serve design, not the other way around. The most exciting future will come when we balance creativity with the right tech strategy.

2. What’s coming up in September?

Here are 3 things I will be doing:

1. Providing FREE access to my 1600+ software ConTech database

I have been collecting new software into a database which I have always wanted to enable access for architects, engineers and construction professionals to search and find the right solutions for them. I have now built front end for this and we’ll be sharing this in future newsletters! This will be a central unique and one of a kind resource and I’m excited to share this!

Image

2. How to move into ConTech FREE resource - helping you move into a new career

Over the past couple of years one of the key things that people ask me is how they move into the construction technology software field. So I thought I would create a resource which helps people to understand what they need to know, training and Resources required, and case studies to show how other people have completed this move. I’ll be sharing this unique resource in September!

Image

Contents include:

  1. Understand the opportunity

  2. Why consider the move?

  3. Key skills to develop

  4. Roadmap steps

  5. Strategic mindset shifts

  6. Resources

  7. Conclusion

3. Sharing FREE resources - AI Tech strategy templates, tech stacks and new software

As always, I will be sharing my thoughts on AI technology, providing templates, example tech stacks and helping you to stay up to date on the AEC ConTech landscape. There are so many exciting things happening in the industry at the moment it can feel overwhelming, I am here to help reduce the noise and enable you to know what is relevant to you.

3. Missed the last Newsletter? Highlights from last month:

If I started an Architecture practice today, here’s the AI Tech Stack I would use…

If I were starting an architecture practice from scratch in 2025, I wouldn’t reach for the same tools that have been around for decades. I’m talking about the legacy software that dominates most studios; AutoCAD, Revit, SketchUp, ArchiCAD. They were game-changing in their time, but let’s be honest: they were all developed before the smartphone, cloud, or AI even existed. They weren’t built for the workflows or expectations of today’s architects, let alone tomorrow’s.

The truth is, you don’t need a bloated suite of disconnected tools to run a modern design practice. You don’t need Revit just to get a project off the ground. You need a tech stack that speaks to each other, automates the boring bits, and supercharges creativity, especially in the critical early stages of design.

That’s why, after assessing over 1,600 software tools through the ADDD Marketplace and working closely with hundreds of architecture and ConTech firms, I’ve put together what I believe is the ideal early-stage AI-powered design stack. 3. Architizer Article published last week!

BIM 2.0: Architectural Design’s Overdue Revolution

Delighted to have an article published in Architizer last week focussing on BIM 2.0 and Generative Design tools. I have summarised this below, but you can read the whole piece here: BIM 2.0: Architectural Design's Overdue Revolution - Architizer Journal

Why Are We Still Using Software from the Last Century?

In an era where AI, automation, and cloud-native tools are reshaping every major industry, architecture remains tethered to legacy software. Most firms still rely on platforms like AutoCAD (1982), ArchiCAD (1987), Revit (1997), Rhino (1998), SketchUp (2000), and Vectorworks (2001), all developed before smartphones, cloud computing, or generative AI were even imagined. These outdated tools force today’s digitally fluent architects into workflows that are slow, siloed, and increasingly unfit for purpose.

The good news? A new wave of platforms under the banner of BIM 2.0 is here, challenging old paradigms and reimagining how early-stage design is done.

The Catalyst for Change

The need for change isn’t new, but it’s now urgent. In 2023, AEC Magazine compared the current software stagnation to a dinosaur extinction event. This was reinforced by the industry’s “Letter to Autodesk,” a public outcry against rising costs and stalled innovation in tools like Revit. These moments catalysed the creation of the Future AEC Software Specification (FASS), a framework outlining what next-generation software must deliver: cloud-first access, real-time collaboration, flexible data workflows, and AI integration.

Image

Giraffe and Fenestra workflow YouTube video

Meet the BIM 2.0 Tools

Today’s emerging platforms align with these FASS principles. They are lean, focused, and designed for the way architects actually work in the early design stages:

  • Arcol – A cloud-based tool simplifying early collaboration across teams.

  • Hypar – Generates layouts and space planning using AI and data.

  • Snaptrude – Delivers real-time design, data capture, and Revit sync.

  • Motif – Enables fast visual collaboration with an ambitious roadmap.

  • Rayon – Makes 2D planning collaborative, rapid, and browser-based.

  • Qonic – Offers fast, intuitive BIM authoring without unnecessary complexity.

These tools aren’t just marginal improvements, they’re working from the ground up to replace outdated design systems. Most are already integrating directly into platforms like Revit, Rhino, and ArchiCAD to enable continuity of design and data.

Image

Generative Design: The Missing Puzzle Piece?

Generative Design, using algorithms to rapidly explore design options, complements BIM 2.0 perfectly. Instead of manually iterating three or four options, architects can now define design goals (like unit mix, height limits, or solar access) and let the software explore thousands of viable outcomes. This accelerates feasibility studies and unlocks faster, smarter decisions early in the process.

Tools like TestFit, Laiout, and Spacio integrate these capabilities, offering AI-driven ideation directly within modelling environments. These aren’t replacing architects, they’re expanding their creative reach.

Image

The Case for Adoption

Together, BIM 2.0 and Generative Design create a new model for early-stage design, faster, more iterative, and deeply collaborative. No more choosing between SketchUp for speed or Revit for data. Now, architects can do both, better.

The benefits are clear:

  • Creativity Unleashed: Rapid iteration and data-driven insight.

  • Collaboration Built-In: Real-time teamwork across platforms.

  • Sustainability by Default: Early feedback on performance metrics.

  • Competitive Edge: Faster feasibility = better chances of winning work.

  • Affordable Access: These tools are priced to encourage experimentation.

Conclusion: The Revolution Has Begun

BIM 2.0 isn’t a trend—it’s a necessary correction. For decades, architectural software has lagged behind the demands of practice. Now, with cloud-native platforms, AI-infused tools, and open connectivity, we finally have a future-facing alternative.

The architects who embrace this shift today won’t just work more efficiently—they’ll lead the next generation of design innovation. It’s time to move on from 20th-century tools and build a profession that’s ready for the 21st.

Welcome to the 7th edition of ADDDitive!

👋 Hi there,

A few years ago, my daughter left a Post-It on my desk:

“Get help.”

It’s stuck with me because it’s true. Growth happens when you bring in the right support at the right time.

I see it all the time: a small practice grows, the “tech-savvy” designer takes on IT, and it works … until it doesn’t. Outdated tools, messy workflows, and siloed data start holding the firm back instead of pushing it forward.

This month’s newsletter is all about spotting the signs your practice needs a Growth-Ready Tech Plan and how to future-proof your workflows.

You’ll also find:

✅ Highlights from our Giraffe + Fenestra webinar

✅ A discount on my Generative Design Report

✅ New ConTech career opportunities & GTM support

Let’s get into it and if this resonates, let’s talk.

Allister

1. Top 5 signs your company needs a Growth-Ready Tech Plan to future-proof your practice:

A few years ago my daughter left this Post-It note on my desk.

Image

I have kept it ever since. Why?

Because it can be interpreted in different ways:

  • At one level it’s a personal critique, suggesting I get support with myself (I have).

  • It is also a commentary that no one can do everything, and seeking help is ok when you don’t know the answer.

  • Lastly, I think it can be about collaboration and having specialists around you to support your growth.

Architects, brilliant as they are, are a case in point.

There are areas that we need help in, and being open and mindful of this can help to grow,

  • Transform, and develop as a practice.

  • As an architect, I see the same pattern play out again and again.

  • A small practice would start to grow.

One of the team, often the most “tech-savvy” designer, would get handed the IT responsibilities.

They’d fix the server, workout why the internet isn't working, and manage the software stack and costs of this.

And it works … for a while.

But when the practice landed bigger projects, the team doubles.

More deadlines, more pressure.

Suddenly, the ageing infrastructure, patchwork of workflows, and ad hoc software choices start to show cracks.

Collaboration became impossible.

Data gets siloed. Deadlines get tighter and harder to meet.

That’s when I realised: without a Growth-Ready Tech Plan, growth starts to hurt.

Top 5 signs your company needs a Growth-Ready Tech Plan to future-proof your practice:

✅ Hardware – Are your machines and devices keeping up with the demands of modern tools?

✅ Infrastructure – Is your network, storage, and cloud setup fit for distributed, secure collaboration?

✅ Software – Are you using the right mix of applications or drowning in overlapping subscriptions?

✅ Workflows – Do your tools actually support the way you work, or do they force bad habits?

✅ AI – Are you starting to integrate AI where it makes sense or missing easy wins?

If this feels familiar, you’re not alone. Many firms wait until it’s painful to tackle these issues but you don’t have to.

Welcome to the 5th edition of ADDDitive!

Hey there 👋,

Thanks for being part of this newsletter, this week I wanted to explore the recent RIBA AI 2025 survey results. I give an overview and why I think that this is sub optimal in terms of their methodology.

I put some more details on my 6 week Technology Strategy, including gap analysis, assessment, hardware, software, infrastructure, processes, and workflows"! I recently helped a practice to explore costs and we found that around $100,000 could be saved from their software costs through better license management.

Book a time with me here: https://meetings-eu1.hubspot.com/allister

AI in Architecture: RIBA Report Insights (and a Reality Check)

The Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) has just dropped its 2025 AI Report, and like many in the industry, I was keen to dive in and understand its key findings. I decided to put the report to the test, tasking four different AI models with breaking down its impact on architects: ChatGPT, Anthropic Claude, Perplexity, and Google Gemini.

The results? Interesting, to say the least.

  • ChatGPT and Perplexity? Couldn't handle the report's size, throwing back error messages.

  • Claude and Gemini successfully processed the information.

  • In my opinion, Gemini offered the sharper, more actionable insights.

You can see a summary of their top takeaways in the carousel below.

Image

However, Here's Where I Have a Problem:

While I applaud RIBA for exploring this crucial topic, I have serious concerns about the report's methodology. Only 500 UK architects responded to the survey, out of a total membership of over 50,000! This equates to less than 1% of the total membership.

What this means is:

  • It's not statistically representative of the industry as a whole. Statements like "60% of architects are using AI" become highly questionable.

  • There may be self-selection bias in that those who responded are likely to have strong opinions or interest in AI (either positive or negative).

  • This survey suffers from incomplete responses in that some questions were skipped, either due to irrelevance or lack of knowledge.

  • This survey is a qualitative direction, not quantitative certainty that This disclaimer suggests the results provide directional insight into professional sentiment rather than statistically robust conclusions.

Image

This lack of representativeness significantly undermines the report's value. I worry that such numbers may be misleading practices and I would like to see a more responsible use of the statistics to help practices understand where they are in context with others.

So, what should we actually do with the RIBA Report?

Here are my suggestions for how RIBA should move forward;

Image

My Thoughts: Actionable Steps for YOUR Architecture Practice

Beyond the report's limitations, AI is undoubtedly transforming architecture. Here are a few key takeaways that practices can and should act on:

  1. Don’t Just Use AI, Understand Where It Fits in Your Workflow: Start by mapping your current workflows, then assess where AI tools can augment, not replace, existing strengths (e.g., feasibility studies or visualisation).

  2. Create a Lightweight AI Policy for Your Practice: Start with a simple internal AI charter. This protects your team and builds client trust.

  3. Focus on Augmentation, Not Automation: Leverage AI for speed and insight, but keep your creative and contextual judgment at the core. Understand how Generative Design helps early stage design.

  4. Start With Use Cases, Not Tools: Too many architects ask, “Which AI should I try?” A better question is, “What problem am I solving?” Pick tools that solve real bottlenecks, not ones that promise vague disruption.

  5. Share and Learn - AI Is Too Big to Navigate Alone: Join peer groups, post your experience (good or bad), and attend webinars.

My Key Takeaway:

The adoption of AI for Architects will only be as good as their holistic Technology Strategy. This involves understanding:

  • Hardware

  • Software

  • Infrastructure

  • Processes

  • Workflows

  • Training

  • Change Management + more

Welcome to the first edition of ADDDitive!

I'm excited to share this curated collection of digital design resources that I've been gathering to help you navigate the increasingly complex technological landscape we all face as architects and designers.

From new marketplace tools to strategic services, upcoming events where we can connect in person, and specialized workflows that could transform your practice—I've focused on actionable intelligence that addresses the real challenges I see practices struggling with every day.

As someone deeply embedded in both the architectural and technology worlds, I'm passionate about bridging these realms to help you build not just better projects, but a more resilient, innovative practice for the future. I hope you'll find something valuable here to implement right away.

New Products on the ADDD Marketplace

This month we have had some amazing new products added to the ADDD Marketplace:

Raven

Raven generates Grasshopper scripts using generative AI. It send your text or image to the romantic technology cloud, and parses the received script directly onto your canvas, using Grasshopper's native components.

Image

Präi

Präi (formerly YANUS.AI) is a SaaS solution that provides a web app-based platform for architectural visualization. It offers seamless plugin integrations with leading architectural software solutions such as Revit, ArchiCAD, Rhino, and SketchUp. This integration allows architects to visualize their models directly from their preferred programs, optimizing the workflow and further enhancing efficiency.

Image

Innex

INNEX is an AI-powered workspace for compliance-driven teams in the built environment. It helps users quickly search, write, review, and collaborate on documents - streamlining complex workflows and ensuring alignment with technical standards.

Image

RenderAI

Turn sketches or text prompts into stunning AI-generated images and videos—fast, easy, and no design experience needed.

Image

Outbuild

Outbuild is an innovative scheduling and field coordination software solution designed to support collaboration between construction teams worldwide.
